title: Roundup: Castleton knocks off D-II SMC | Local | rutlandherald.com
text:
RUTLAND TOWN — The Vermont State University Castleton men's hockey team earned a 3-2 overtime win against Division II St. Michael's College Wednesday night at Spartan Arena.
St. Michael's jumped out to a 2-0 lead in the second period after a scoreless opening period with goals by AJ Sacco and Brayden Naumann.
Castleton tied the game in the third period with two goals by Tyler Burke. Marcus Bellomo assisted on both goals, while Joey Ala and Cole Bowditch had an assist apiece.
Luke Chakrabarti continued his standout campaign with the game-winner in overtime, assisted by Cam Reid and Emmett McHardy.
Charles Watson had 31 saves for the Spartans, while Cole Manahan stopped an incredible 62 shots in the loss for the Purple Knights.
Castleton (5-5-1) looks to push above the .500 mark at Skidmore College on Wednesday. SMC (3-4-3) is at Franklin Pierce on Friday.
FIELD HOCKEY
NFHCA honors
COLORADO SPRINGS, Colo. — Jess Smithson of the Vermont State University Castleton field hockey team was named a National Field Hockey Coaches Association (NFHCA) 2025 Division III All-Region selection on Wednesday morning.
Smithson earned Second Team honors to cap a stellar career as a Spartan, posting a career-best 11 defensive saves—second-most in the Little East Conference. The Beckingham, England native also contributed offensively with 12 points (5g, 2a), ranking third on the squad.
She adds the All-Region accolade to an impressive list of achievements this season, including NFHCA Collegiate Senior Team selection, All-LEC First Team honors, and her second consecutive LEC Defensive Player of the Year award.
Smithson graduates with three All-LEC First Team selections, two NFHCA All-Region honors, two LEC Defensive Player of the Year awards, and four LEC Defensive Player of the Week recognitions. She is tied for eighth in career assists (23) in the Castleton record book.
Three members of the Middlebury College field hockey team have been selected to the National Field Hockey Coaches Association (NFHCA) All-Region II teams. Megan Fuqua and Grace Keefe were first-team selections, while Tessa Herbst earned a second-team nod.
Fuqua collects her initial all-region honor. The forward earned All-NESCAC distinction with a spot on the first team.
She was a key contributor to the Panther attack, leading the squad with 30 points and 14 goals.
The midfielder had three multi-goal contests, including four scores against then-No. 3 Babson and during the opening round of the NCAA Tournament in a triumph over Westfield State.
Fuqua finished the season with points in three of the last five contests.
She had three game-winning tallies, headlined by the go-ahead goal in a 3-2 come-from-behind victory over #8 Endicott in the second round of the NCAA Tournament.
Keefe tallies her first career all-region accolade. The defender was also named an All-NESCAC First-Team honoree.
Keefe finished third in minutes played (1,238) this fall, appearing in all 20 contests with 19 starts.
The Panther had two crucial defensive saves that helped seal Middlebury's 2-1 win over then-#6 Bates in the regular season.
Keefe contributed on the offensive end, recording 12 points with four goals and four assists. She caps her Middlebury career with 30 points coming from 11 goals and eight assists in 2,223 minutes.
Herbst grabs her inaugural regional honor from the NFHCA. The Panther was tabbed to the All-NESCAC Second Team.
She was a stalwart for the Panther defensive unit, leading the team with 1,336 minutes. The defender was one of four players to start all 20 matchups.
Herbst helped pace a program that led the conference and ranked 14th in Division III in goals against average (0.94) and shut out six opponents.
She contributed two assists on the offensive end and was part of a penalty corner unit that ranked second in the nation, securing 11.40 per contest.
